title: MA2H Submit Ack (v0.5)
description: Body of the 202 Accepted returned by POST /v1/messages. v0.5 lists two additions for the addressed (inter-agent) path: `status: queued` and the `destination` reachability snapshot — this schema is closed (additionalProperties: false), so both are deliberate, listed changes (spec §8.1; SCP #24 Backward compatibility).

status.description: The verb's OWNING-track status (spec §8.1; per spec §1 this is 'open, delivered, or a terminal value'). At first accept: `open` for ANY ask/task, addressed or not (the §7 resolution track — `open` asserts nothing about delivery); `delivered` for a human-inbox notify; `queued` for an ADDRESSED notify only (its lifecycle IS the §14.2 delivery track, and asserting `delivered` at accept would be the false belief v0.5 bans). An idempotent same-payload replay returns the original ack with the owning track's CURRENT status (spec §8.1) — e.g. `bounced`/`expired` for an addressed notify, a §7 resolution for an ask/task.

destination.description: REQUIRED on the ack for EVERY addressed submit, any verb (v0.5, spec §8.1): the destination's reachability at send time, and the sender's misroute detector — its absence on an addressed-submit ack means a pre-0.5 Hub misrouted the message to the human inbox, which the sender MUST treat as a failure. Schema-enforceable only for the unambiguously-addressed statuses (`queued`/`bounced`, the allOf below): `open` also occurs on the human-inbox path, so for an addressed ask/task's `open` ack the requirement is Hub-enforced, a §12 downstream-proof obligation — the sender-side detector never depends on the schema (the sender knows it addressed the message). When the sender lacks visibility for the destination, exactly {"state": "unknown"} with no last_seen (schema-enforced below, mirroring presence.schema.json).

allOf.$comment: queued and bounced are unambiguously ADDRESSED statuses, so the §8.1 destination MUST applies — its absence is the misroute signal. expired/cancelled/etc. stay unconditional: they also occur on the human-inbox path.
